tasks.do: The hop (CK-71, Zafar 9 Nov, his words in the row): the round's items sit whole in the bottom band (the shared shelf's tray and word pills, as in every other game; the board above the band, ART-37), each in its slot. They hop straight up out of the band onto the board, hang a moment, and drop back into their slot, at different times (no arcs, nothing from off-screen). A swipe across an item while it is up cuts it in two (the existing slice, halves and sound); a cut item's halves land on the board and stay. A swipe on a decoy is a gentle no (the existing feedback), never a verdict. Decoys hop as often as targets so the hop never gives the answer away (the leak test).
tasks.accept: a script-made frame strip of one hop (up, hang, cut, halves) at 930x430 and 740x320; grep: no arc path left in the chop mechanic

tasks.do: Levels: L1 one item up at a time, one kind, no decoys; L2 two up at a time, one sometimes a decoy; L3 and L4 more at once and faster, from the settings' knobs (data/stations/chop.json) and the central decoy rules. The ring, the order card, the redo of a short count and the round's end stay as they are.

tasks.do: Fairness for a 3-6 year old: an item stays up long enough to swipe at L1 (at least 1.5 s, the knob in the settings), the swipe's catch area is the item's whole picture plus a margin, and a child who taps instead of swiping still cuts at L1 (a tap counts as a chop there). Nothing waits on speech.
